title: Apple's Foldable iPhone Duo Screens Are Cracking Within Hours, Owners Say
excerpt: Early buyers of the $1,999 iPhone Duo report inner displays splitting along the fold with an audible snap. Apple says a small number of units are affected and is replacing them through AppleCare, without naming a cause or a count.
body:
• Owners of Apple's first foldable phone, the $1,999 iPhone Duo, have reported its inner display cracking along the fold within hours or days of use, accompanied by an audible pop or snap and bright lines of pixels.
  • Apple has said it is "aware of an issue impacting the inner display on a small number of iPhone Duo units" and advised affected customers to contact AppleCare for replacements; it has disclosed neither a cause nor a count.
  • Repair firm iFixit's analysis, reported by Techstrong IT, points to stress around the central hinge support bar and flex cables — a theory Apple has not confirmed.
  • If your Duo's inner screen cracks, Apple's stated route is AppleCare for a replacement — but Gizbot reported some stores do not have stock for an immediate swap, so expect a possible wait.

Apple's first foldable iPhone has run into an early durability problem. Within days of the iPhone Duo reaching buyers, owners began posting photos and video of cracked inner displays, and the reports have since drawn a nickname in online tech communities: "crackgate." The device unfolds book-style to a 7.6-inch inner display and starts at nearly $2,000, according to Techstrong IT's reporting.

What owners are reporting

The failure pattern described across reports is consistent. Multiple users documented hearing an audible pop or snap while operating the hinge, followed by physical cracking along the fold line and vertical rows of distorted or brightly lit pixels, Techstrong IT reported. The iPhone Duo's reference page similarly records white lines extending across the screen, an audible cracking sound while opening or closing the phone, and some owners reporting the display breaking after a few hours of use. The phone went on sale on October 23, 2026.

Gizbot reported that Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, in his Power On newsletter, said he had independently verified reports of cracked displays on devices used normally by customers, and that the number of affected units could be in the thousands — a figure Gizbot itself flagged as a reported estimate, not a confirmed count. In India, the iPhone Duo starts at Rs 2,99,900, Gizbot reported, with limited availability pushing some grey-market sellers to ask Rs 50,000 to Rs 1 lakh over the official price.

Apple's response

"We are aware of an issue impacting the inner display on a small number of iPhone Duo units."

https://x.com/TMA_MarketIntel/status/2116923000960491734 — Apple, in a statement reported by Techstrong IT and Gizbot

Apple advised affected customers to contact AppleCare for replacements, and Techstrong IT reported that several owners said store personnel swapped their broken hardware on the spot. Beyond that, the company's public position is thin: Gizbot reported Apple has not shared an exact figure for affected units, has not explained what is causing the damage, and has not announced a public recall. Apple has also said the issue appears relatively quickly on affected devices rather than developing gradually, Gizbot reported.

Getting a replacement may not be immediate. The Duo has faced supply constraints since launch, and some Apple Stores reportedly do not have enough stock to provide an immediate swap, leaving affected users waiting for another unit, Gizbot reported. It also reported that Apple has issued guidance to stores and authorised service providers on identifying and handling affected devices, with technicians instructed to inspect the phone and follow standard repair or replacement procedures.

A possible cause — unconfirmed

Repair authority iFixit constructed a 3-D hinge model using patents, teardown footage and CT scans to pinpoint structural stress points, Techstrong IT reported. Its findings indicated the central support bar appears to struggle to drop sufficiently as the device closes, concentrating pressure where the crossing flex cables meet the central hinge, and that fine powder quickly penetrates the internal moving parts. That is iFixit's theory from teardown analysis, not a cause Apple has confirmed.

https://www.instagram.com/p/Dd9S1_0miad/

Independent testing added to the questions. In a live-streamed stress test by Polish technology reviewer Kuba Klawiter, the iPhone Duo failed after 75,003 folds following exposure to ambient dust and freezing temperatures, developing lines identical to consumer damage reports, Techstrong IT reported. Dan O'Brien, president and chief operating officer of The Futurum Group, told the outlet that user acceptance of foldables is still nascent and devices need to last two to three years without issues before mass adoption is possible.

What happens next

The open questions are the size of the affected batch and the cause. Apple maintains the defect is confined to a small fraction of units; the reporting so far cannot size it, and no source has established whether replacement units carry the same vulnerability. Until Apple publishes a cause or a service programme, an affected owner's practical step is the one Apple itself stated: contact AppleCare, and be prepared for a wait if local replacement stock is short.
